title: zazzle invoker use cases
description: Running a zazzle command from a shell.

entities.name: Run a zazzle command in a shell
entities.description: A coding agent runs `zazzle CMD ...` (or `zazz CMD ...`, or an installed zazz script by its name); the invoker hands the command to the daemon, starting it if needed, and exits with the daemon's status, or becomes the program that runs it.
entities.goal: Get a command's answer on its own standard output, as cheaply as running any small program.
preconditions: zazzle runs on macOS arm64 or Linux x86_64/aarch64.
A daemon listens on the socket, or zazzled is beside zazzle (or named by ZAZZLE_DAEMON) so zazzle can start one.
postconditions: The command's text is on zazzle's standard output, or its error on standard error, written there by the daemon (or by the program zazzle became).
zazzle's exit status is the daemon's status byte (0 or 2 for zazzle and zazz commands; a zazz script run as a command answers with its own exit status), or that program's own status.

flow.action: Runs `zazzle CMD ARGS` in its shell, with ZAZZLE_SESSION set to a stable id if it wants ids, dedupe and read-again.

Looks at the name it was started under and at CMD: free-disk-space, fix-network, proxy and run (each only as zazzle) are not daemon requests; anything else is, so `zazz run NAME` and a script's own `run` argument reach the daemon.

Builds the request: an empty working-directory field, the session from ZAZZLE_SESSION, then `zazz` when it runs as zazz, or `zazz exec-name NAME` when it runs under any other name NAME, then its arguments; and the socket path from ZAZZLE_SOCK or $HOME/.zazzle/sock.
Checks the process on the other end runs as the same user.
Opens its working directory and sends the request with descriptors 0, 1, 2 and that directory attached to the first message.
Polls for the one status byte the daemon sends after writing the answer to the passed streams, for up to 25 µs without sleeping, then blocks on it, and exits with it.

alternatives.outcome: zazzle replaces itself with the binary of that name in its own directory, with the remaining arguments; no daemon is contacted, and the tool's streams and exit status are the caller's. If it cannot be run: `cannot run the tool (error N)`, exit 69.

alternatives.condition: CMD is run or proxy and the invoker runs as zazzle.
alternatives.outcome: zazzle replaces itself with `zazzled wrap ARGS` or `zazzled proxy ARGS` (ZAZZLE_DAEMON, or the zazzled beside it), keeping the caller's environment, streams and exit status. If it cannot be run: `cannot run zazzled (error N)`, exit 69.

alternatives.condition: zazzle runs as `zazz`, or under another name (a shim made by `zazz install`), and CMD is not run or proxy.
alternatives.outcome: The request goes to the daemon's zazz command: `zazz ARGS`, or `zazz exec-name NAME ARGS` for a shim, which runs that installed script with the caller's streams and answers with its exit status; free-disk-space and fix-network are passed on as arguments, not exec'd.

alternatives.condition: The arguments do not fit the 256 KiB request buffer.
HOME is unset (and ZAZZLE_SOCK too), or the socket path is too long for a socket address.
alternatives.outcome: `HOME is not set` or `socket path too long`, exit 78.

alternatives.condition: Nothing listens (no socket file, or connection refused).
alternatives.outcome: Starts ZAZZLE_DAEMON, or the zazzled beside its own executable, as `zazzled serve` in a new session with its standard streams on /dev/null, then retries after 2 ms, doubling the wait up to 128 ms, for up to 3 s, and goes on to check-uid.

alternatives.condition: The daemon cannot be started, does not listen within 3 s, or connecting fails another way.
alternatives.outcome: `cannot start daemon (error N)`, `daemon did not start` or `cannot connect to daemon`, exit 69.

alternatives.condition: The daemon runs as another user.
alternatives.outcome: `daemon runs as another user`, exit 77; nothing is sent.

alternatives.condition: The working directory cannot be opened, or sending fails.
alternatives.outcome: `cannot open cwd`, exit 66, or `send failed`, exit 74.

alternatives.condition: The daemon closes the connection without a status byte.
